extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and research organizations (universities, national laboratories, non-profit organizations, private firms) interested in applying for DOE EFRC funding
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement/overview of a DOE Funding Opportunity Announcement (EFRC competition) describing topical focus areas, who is eligible to apply, expected award sizes and duration, and the selection process. Intended to guide institutions preparing proposals for Energy Frontier Research Centers in the specified topical areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical focus areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Centers under this initiative will support fundamental research projects in four topical areas: quantum information science, microelectronics, environmental management and polymer upcycling (developing the chemistry to convert waste plastics into fuels and other high-value products).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target one of these four topical areas; polymer upcycling is explicitly defined as developing chemistry to convert waste plastics into fuels and other high-value products. The program emphasizes fundamental research that can underpin future energy and environmental management technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose / research scope
rubrics_metrics.description: To accelerate scientific advances in materials science, chemistry, geosciences, and biosciences and to provide the scientific foundation for future advances in energy and environmental management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed center research should align with DOE’s mission to advance foundational science in the listed disciplines and demonstrate relevance to energy and/or environmental management outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities, national laboratories, nonprofit organizations, and private firms are eligible to compete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to form multi-disciplinary research teams that may include partnerships with other institutions; consortia or collaborations across sectors are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal and new center eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The competition will be open to proposals both from existing EFRCs seeking renewal of support (in the environmental management topical area) and from institutions seeking to establish new EFRCs under the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing EFRCs may seek renewal specifically in the environmental management topical area; other topical-area renewals are not described on this announcement. New center proposals are solicited for any of the four topical areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection will be based on a rigorous peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement references peer review as the basis for selection but does not detail review criteria on this page; applicants should consult the full Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) for review criteria and scoring guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected award size and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards for each selected center are expected to range from $2 million to $4 million per year for a planned total of four fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is provided annually within the $2M–$4M range and continuation for the planned four-year period is contingent on congressional appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on multidisciplinary, high-performing teams
rubrics_metrics.description: “These centers bring together the nation’s leading scientists in dynamic, innovative teams across multiple disciplines,” the announcement states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should assemble teams that demonstrate disciplinary breadth, leading expertise, and the capacity for innovative, collaborative research; partnerships with other institutions are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected outputs / contribution to DOE mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Since their establishment by DOE’s Office of Science in 2009, the EFRCs have produced thousands of peer-reviewed scientific publications and continue to be an important asset to the Department’s mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be positioned to generate high-quality, peer-reviewed research outputs and demonstrably advance DOE’s scientific and mission objectives; historical productivity is framed as a program expectation.
